newsitem.title: UAE: EDI seen as vital tool for air cargo industry.
newsitem.headline: EDI seen as vital tool for air cargo industry.

text.p: Electronic data interchange (EDI) is an essential and strategic tool for the survival of the air cargo industry, an air cargo consultant said on Monday.

Robert Wagner, an independent consultant speaking at an air cargo conference in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, said EDI could help the air freight industry cope with declining market shares, cargo tracking problems, costly administration and low rates of efficiency.

"EDI is a miracle cure," Wagner told delegates on the final day of the two-day conference. "EDI generates savings for all partners in the transportation chain...improves the quality of service...(and) helps the industry become more efficient."
Wagner said EDI would also improve the cycle time of shipments by 40 percent while reducing shipping errors by up to 30 percent.
He said electronic data processing would also enhance productivity and reduce inventories which are costly to maintain.
The estimated savings in international trade through the use of EDI was "three to seven percent of the total value of traded goods, which translates into several billion U.S. dollars," Wagner said.
He said a pilot project for a paperless air waybill (AWB) showed that handling could be cut from 30 minutes with manual handling to six minutes with the use of EDI.
Wagner said the savings with an electronic AWB could be dramatic.

"UPS (United Parcel Service) made a survey...and found that by reducing the number of AWB copies by one, this would result in reduction of costs for paper, printing, filing and save an estimated $56 million per year," he said.

EDI can help improve communication between shippers and transport providers, whether freight forwarders or airlines. It can also enable customers and transporters to check the location of a parcel at any point in time.
"EDI benefits always exceed their costs," Wagner said.

The cargo conference is hosted by the Sharjah Airport Authority and organised by the Airports Council International, a world organisation for airports. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
